question: Who was appointed as the first woman Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Santishree Pandit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In February 2022, **Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit **made history as the **first woman Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) in Delhi**, appointed by the Ministry of Education. 
 
• She is an alumna of JNU, holds an MPhil and PhD in International Relations from the university. 
 
• Currently serving as the Vice Chancellor of Savitribai Phule University in Maharashtra, she brings a wealth of experience, having also served on prestigious bodies such as the University Grants Commission (UGC) and the Indian Council of Social Science Research (ICSSR), in addition to being a Visitor's nominee to central universities. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• Indian development economist** Jayati Ghosh **has been selected by UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to join a new high-level advisory board on effective multilateralism.
 
• **Utsa Patnaik, **a retired professor of economics from Jawaharlal Nehru University, received the Malcolm Adiseshiah Award in April 2023. This award, established by UNESCO in 1998, recognizes outstanding contributions to education and literacy. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jawaharlal Nehru University,** a renowned public research institution located in Delhi, India, was established in 1969 through an act of parliament. 
 
• Named after India's first Prime Minister, Jawaharlal Nehru, the university's founding vice-chancellor was G. Parthasarathy, with Prof. Moonis Raza serving as the Founder Chairman and Rector. 
 
• The bill for its establishment was introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 1 September 1965 by the then-Minister of Education, M. C. Chagla.
